name.text: Derive the quadratic formula — order the steps (drag and drop)

questiontext.text:
The steps below derive the quadratic formula for \(a x^2 + b x + c = 0\) (with \(a \neq 0\)) by completing the square, but they have been shuffled.

Drag each step from the right-hand list into the box on the left so that, read from top to bottom, they form a correct and logical derivation.

[[parsons input="ans1"]] {# parsons_encode(proof_steps) #} [[/parsons]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Each step follows from the previous one. The key idea is to reach a perfect square on the left before taking square roots.

\[ \begin{align*} a x^2 + b x + c &= 0 &&\text{(standard form)}\\ x^2 + \tfrac{b}{a}x + \tfrac{c}{a} &= 0 &&\text{(divide by } a\text{)}\\ x^2 + \tfrac{b}{a}x &= -\tfrac{c}{a} &&\text{(move the constant)}\\ x^2 + \tfrac{b}{a}x + \left(\tfrac{b}{2a}\right)^2 &= -\tfrac{c}{a} + \left(\tfrac{b}{2a}\right)^2 &&\text{(complete the square)}\\ \left(x+\tfrac{b}{2a}\right)^2 &= \tfrac{b^2-4ac}{4a^2} &&\text{(factor and combine)}\\ x + \tfrac{b}{2a} &= \pm\tfrac{\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} &&\text{(take square roots)}\\ x &= -\tfrac{b}{2a} \pm \tfrac{\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} &&\text{(isolate } x\text{)}\\ x &= \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} &&\text{(single fraction)} \end{align*} \]

prtcorrect.text: Correct — that is a valid derivation of the quadratic formula.

node.description: Is the student's ordering equivalent to the correct derivation?

falsefeedback.text:
Not the correct order yet. Work through the logic in stages:

  • first make the leading coefficient \(1\) by dividing by \(a\);
  • then move the constant to the right so the \(x\)-terms are alone;
  • complete the square, and only take square roots once the left-hand side is a perfect square;
  • finally isolate \(x\) and write the result as a single fraction.

qtest.description: Wrong order (divide before writing standard form, and root before completing)
